SCOPE OF WHAT I READ FIRST-HAND vs INFERRED — this matters for the strictness rules:
- READ FIRST-HAND: every hit count, every title, and the complete abstract text for ~60 records (efetch rettype=abstract), plus the raw XML metadata for the 5 priority papers. Every quoted sentence in the results above is a verbatim string from an abstract I retrieved.
- NOT READ: no full texts. PubMed does not host full text, so for records whose abstract names complement as a measured endpoint WITHOUT stating the outcome, I recorded the outcome as UNVERIFIED rather than guessing. The two most important such cases are PMID 27854228 (PMO/eteplirsen NHP — "complement alternative pathway" listed as an endpoint, result not in abstract; do NOT score as negative) and PMID 26210642 (ISIS-APO(a)Rx phase 1 — "complement variables" measured, result not in abstract).
- INFERRED (and labelled as such): classification of each record into human_clinical / human_laboratory / animal / mechanistic_only / target_is_complement_efficacy is my judgement from the abstract text, not a claim the paper self-labels that way.

HIGHEST-VALUE NOVEL FINDS, ranked:
1. PMID 27739230 (ARC-520, healthy human volunteers) — a positive, prospectively measured "low-level, transient complement induction" in humans given an RNAi therapeutic. This is a genuinely new human clinical datapoint and is NOT in the context set.
2. PMID 26210642 (ISIS-APO(a)Rx phase 1) — human clinical with complement measured as a declared safety variable AND a trial identifier (EudraCT 2012-004909-27, not an NCT), which partially answers the context's "Crooke 2016 has no trial identifiers" gap.
3. PMID 9034989 (LJP 394 / abetimus sodium, SLE patients) — human clinical, transient increases in complement split products after IV oligonucleotide. Confound: SLE baseline complement consumption.
4. PMID 9873494 — a second, separate human in-vitro complement experiment comparing PS-DNA against PS-RNA / 2'-OMe-RNA / 2'-5'-RNA, i.e. a chemistry-dependence dataset in human complement.
5. PMID 27140858 — chronic-dosing monkey data showing PROGRESSIVE rises in basal Bb and C3a and SUSTAINED C3 depletion, which is kinetically different from the single-dose picture in the context set.
6. PMID 28123102 — minipig, a species beyond the monkey/human axis of the context set.
7. PMID 37093125 — explicitly dissociates platelet-surface C3d/C4d deposition from fluid-phase alternative-pathway activation; an endpoint-definition caution.
8. PMID 31881528 — same chemistry and length, different sequence, complement activation abolished: sequence-dependence evidence.

PROPERLY-QUALIFIED NEGATIVES (measured non-activation, which per the rules is distinct from "unreported"): PMID 11446591 (INX-3280, no complement change despite Cmax ABOVE the published activation threshold — the strongest of these), PMID 18766340 (STAT3 decoy, Bb measured, no AP activation, cynomolgus), PMID 26048585 (E-selectin aptamer, C3a and C5a measured, unchanged, mouse), PMID 35737426 (SLN360 siRNA, no complement activation in vivo), PMID 24720569 (IMT504: slight total-complement change BUT explicit no alternative-pathway activation — do not collapse these two statements).

ATTRIBUTION CAUTION I want to flag to the parent: PMID 12429653 (LErafAON) reports large complement changes (total hemolytic complement down ~62-74%, C3a ~3-fold, Bb ~5-12-fold) but states these occurred "in LErafAON AND BLANK LIPOSOME groups". Likewise PMID 29191134 (LNP-mRNA), PMID 15264853 (PEI-g-PEG) and PMID 10411464 (ATTA8-DSPE liposomes) show complement activation driven by the DELIVERY VEHICLE. For any formulated product (including CALAA-01 in the context set) the oligonucleotide and the carrier cannot be assumed to be the same cause.

STRICT SEPARATION APPLIED: sefaxersen (PMIDs 39893955, 41443406, 42713733, 42718940), cemdisiran (42030965), the C5 GalNAc-siRNA (42596551), factor B ASOs (28855795, 26307001), avacincaptad pegol (32882310, 41407269), the factor B-binding DNA aptamers (33419768, 39431879) and the complement-targeting oligonucleotide hydrogel microspheres (41312643) all measure complement as EFFICACY pharmacodynamics. I have labelled every one target_is_complement_efficacy and kept them out of the toxicity evidence tally. The two factor-B aptamer papers are nonetheless mechanistically interesting for the toxicity endpoint because they show the same oligonucleotide backbone class binding an alternative-pathway component at picomolar affinity.

Europe PMC (https://europepmc.org/) \u20.applicability_justification: Highly applicable and the single most productive resource searched so far. Field-restricted queries (TITLE:, ABSTRACT:, METHODS:, JOURNAL:, SRC:, HAS_SUPPL:) collapse hit counts from hundreds of review-noise results to 3-70 precise results. The API surfaced 16 novel toxicity-relevant primary studies plus 9 target-is-complement efficacy studies, and the /fullTextXML + /supplementaryFiles endpoints let me verify analyte names, licences, trial identifiers and raw-data contents FIRST-HAND rather than inferring them. Concretely: I retrieved and parsed Sewing 2017's actual supplementary workbook through the API, and I extracted the exact complement analytes from six full texts. Two caveats learned by running the queries: (a) unrestricted boolean queries sort newest-first and flood with 2026 reviews, so hit counts are not a relevance signal; (b) the word "complement" used as an ordinary verb ("to complement this assessment", "complement UFH", "complement oligodeoxynucleotide-mediated adjuvanticity") is a major false-positive source — it is why PMID 36579950 and PMID 35021888 matched and both are not relevant.

relevant_results.title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacokinetics of ARC-520 Injection, an RNA Interference-Based Therapeutic for the Treatment of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection, in Healthy Volunteers
relevant_results.why_relevant: READ FIRST-HAND (full text via /fullTextXML). Highest-value novel find: a human clinical complement dataset for an siRNA therapeutic that is absent from the context. Methods, verbatim: 'Venous blood samples were collected and processed to produce serum (for complement CH50 analysis) or plasma (for split products-Bb analysis).' Results, verbatim: 'An increase in individual Bb levels (a measure of alternative pathway activation) was detected beginning in cohort 3 (1 subject) and cohort 4 (1 subject)'; 'A pattern of Bb increase was seen in the cohort average for groups 6, 7, 8, and 9'; 'In all cases, the increase in Bb occurred at 0.5 and 2 hours postdose'; 'in cohort 9, there was a pattern toward a decrease in CH50 at 2 hours postdose in 4 subjects (3 treated with ARC-520 Injection, 1 treated with placebo)'. Abstract conclusion: 'Low-level, transient complement induction and sporadic, mild, and transient elevations of several cytokines were observed but not associated with any symptoms.' Trial identifier extracted first-hand from text: Heparc-1001, NCT01872065, single centre Nucleus Network Melbourne, 9 sequential cohorts, recruitment from July 2013, database closure October 2014. Licence cc by-nc-nd (API field). Unlike Crooke 2016 this paper DOES carry its trial identifier. NOT a complement-targeting drug: ARC-520 targets HBV transcripts, so this is toxicity/safety pharmacodynamics.

relevant_results.title: Integrated Assessment of the Clinical Performance of GalNAc3-Conjugated 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Chimeric Antisense Oligonucleotides: I. Human Volunteer Experience
relevant_results.why_relevant: READ FIRST-HAND (full text via /fullTextXML). Second major novel human clinical complement dataset. Methods, verbatim: 'Samples were collected before dosing for standard clinical laboratory tests and collected at several time points within a 24-h period after SC dose administration for coagulation tests and complement split products.' Figure legend, verbatim: 'Mean laboratory measurements of coagulation and complement activation over the 24-h period postdose 1 in single and weekly multidose regimen cohorts, (a) activated partial thromboplastin time, (b) prothrombin time, (c) complement split product Bb, and (d) complement split product C5a.' This is an explicit human NEGATIVE (measured and non-activating), not an 'unreported'. Pools several GalNAc3-2'MOE ASO programmes; target abbreviations listed in the paper include AGT, ANGPTL3, APOC3, CFB (complement factor B), GHR, HBV S, KLKB1 and LPA. Cohort n values appearing in the safety table row: 36, 121, 32, 38, 33, 12, 6. Licence cc by-nc (API field). NOTE the mixed-intent trap: one pooled programme targets CFB, where complement reduction is efficacy; but Bb and C5a here are measured as SAFETY endpoints across the whole platform, so the dataset belongs on the toxicity side with that caveat flagged. relevant_results.title: Effects of Repeated Complement Activation Associated with Chronic Treatment of Cynomolgus Monkeys with 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Modified Antisense Oligonucleotide
relevant_results.why_relevant: Abstract READ FIRST-HAND via resultType=core. The single most detailed chronic-dosing complement toxicology study found anywhere in this resource, and absent from the context. ISIS 104838, up to 9 months, total 30 mg/kg/week given as 4.3 mg/kg/day s.c., or 30 mg/kg once weekly s.c., or 30 mg/kg 30-min i.v. infusion. Verbatim: 'Acute elevations of complement split products (Bb and C3a) and a transient decrease in C3 occurred after the first dose and were drug plasma concentration dependent. However, with repeated complement activation after chronic ASO treatment, there were progressive increases in basal (predose) levels of Bb and C3a, and a sustained C3 reduction in all treated groups. There was also a progressive increase in C3d-bound circulating immune complex (CIC) that was considered secondary to the C3 depletion.' Vascular inflammation in liver, kidney and heart correlated with severe C3 depletion. The authors' own caveat, verbatim: 'based on the known sensitivity of monkeys to ASO-induced complement activation, these findings have limited relevance to humans.' Not OA (isOpenAccess=N, no PMC); full text not retrieved, so sub-abstract numbers are UNVERIFIED.
relevant_results.complement_analytes: Bb, C3a, C3, C3d-bound circulating immune complex

relevant_results.title: Complement C3d/C4d Deposition on Platelets Correlates with 2'-O-Methoxyethyl Antisense Oligonucleotide-Induced Thrombocytopenia in Monkeys
relevant_results.why_relevant: Abstract READ FIRST-HAND via resultType=core. Novel, and mechanistically distinct from every other item: measures CELL-BOUND complement rather than fluid-phase split products. ISIS 405879, 40 mg/kg/week for 16 weeks, induced severe thrombocytopenia (platelets <50 K/uL) in seven of nine Mauritian-sourced cynomolgus monkeys but not in Asian-sourced animals. Verbatim: 'Marked increases in PLT-bound C3d/C4d were detected in all thrombocytopenic Mauritian-sourced monkeys but not in the unaffected Mauritian- or Asian-sourced monkeys, suggesting increased PLT clearance due to complement deposition on the PLTs. However, this effect was independent of the ASO-mediated fluid-phase alternative complement activation.' That last clause is important for the endpoint: it dissociates platelet-surface complement deposition from the classic fluid-phase alternative-pathway readout. Also reports anti-GPIIb/IIIa IgG correlating with platelet reduction, and increases in total serum IgM, anti-platelet IgM and anti-PF4 IgM. Not OA, no PMC; full text not retrieved.
relevant_results.complement_analytes: platelet-bound C3d/C4d (cell-surface, not fluid-phase)

relevant_results.title: Single-dose hemodynamic toxicity and pharmacokinetics of a partial phosphorothioate anti-HIV oligonucleotide (AR177) after intravenous infusion to cynomolgus monkeys
relevant_results.why_relevant: Abstract READ FIRST-HAND via resultType=core. Novel, and valuable because of the unusual chemistry: AR177 (zintevir) is a 17-mer with a PHOSPHODIESTER backbone carrying single phosphorothioate linkages only at the 3' and 5' ends — sequence given in the abstract as 5' GTGGTGGGTGGGTGGGT-3'. Single 10-minute i.v. infusions of 5, 20 or 50 mg/kg or saline. Verbatim: 'There was a minimal, dose-dependent increase in the levels of complement split product Bb and total hemolytic complement.' So a near-fully-phosphodiester, G-quartet-forming oligonucleotide still produced a dose-dependent Bb rise — relevant to apportioning the effect between backbone chemistry and higher-order structure. 'Total hemolytic complement' is the CH50-type functional readout the task asked about. Note the direction as written is an INCREASE in total hemolytic complement, unlike the CH50 decrease seen in ARC-520; I am reporting the sentence as written and not reconciling the two. Not OA, no PMC; full text not retrieved.
relevant_results.complement_analytes: Bb; total hemolytic complement

relevant_results.title: Preclinical toxicity and toxicokinetics of GTI-2040, a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide targeting ribonucleotide reductase R2

Europe PMC (https://europepmc.org/) \u20.notes:
BOTTOM LINE: Europe PMC was the most productive resource so far. 24 distinct query formulations, all executed successfully, no access barrier to the resource. Yield: 16 novel toxicity-relevant primary studies (2 human clinical, 13 animal, 1 CpG/mouse), 9 novel target-is-complement efficacy studies kept strictly separate, and first-hand verification of the licence, data-availability and supplement status of all four priority papers.

THE TWO FINDINGS THAT MOST CHANGE THE PICTURE:
1. PMID 27739230 / PMC5516171 — ARC-520, NCT01872065. A human clinical complement dataset (Bb in plasma, CH50 in serum) for an siRNA therapeutic, with a real trial identifier, entirely absent from the context. The context's human clinical tier was Crooke 2016 (no identifiers) + Demirjian + regulatory-report-only compounds. This adds a citable, identifier-bearing, OA human dataset showing low-level transient alternative-pathway activation.
2. PMID 30570431 / PMC6386089 — GalNAc3-2'MOE ASO integrated human volunteer experience, measuring Bb and C5a, reporting an explicit measured NEGATIVE across single and multidose cohorts. A measured human non-activation is scientifically distinct from "unreported" and the endpoint needs both poles.

ON THE COMMIT-SEWING-ONLY DECISION, which this search supports on three independent grounds: Sewing is the ONLY one of the four priority papers whose raw data is both openly licensed (CC BY 4.0, confirmed twice) and machine-retrievable (the /supplementaryFiles endpoint serves pone.0187574.s001.xlsx, 54,955 bytes, HTTP 200). Mangsbo's API routes are both closed (fullTextXML HTTP 500; supplementaryFiles returns "not open access") and it carries no CC licence at all. Crooke's supplement is one 1.9 MB PDF with figures as images. Demirjian's supplement is two CONSORT .doc files. None of the four has any repository deposit — hasDbCrossReferences=N for every one, and hasTMAccessionNumbers=Y only for ARC-520 (that flag is picking up the NCT, not a data accession).

ON THE ANTICOAGULANT CONVENTION: de Boer 2022 uses LEPIRUDIN-anticoagulated human whole blood and plasma, read first-hand from the abstract. This is the complement-compatible choice (citrate and EDTA chelate the divalent cations complement activation requires), so adopting lepirudin as the stated convention is consistent with the closest human whole-blood comparator. Flag, though: the convention should be recorded PER DATASET rather than assumed uniform, because I could not verify Sewing's or Mangsbo's anticoagulant from what I retrieved, and a cross-study comparison of absolute C3a/C5a across different anticoagulants would not be sound.

VERIFIED NUMERIC CHECK ON THE COMMITTED DATASET: the context's "144 per-donor stimulation-index values in sheet Figure 6" is EXACTLY RIGHT, but only for the complement subset — C3a block 72 values + C5a block 72 values. The sheet as a whole holds 380 numeric cells because it also stacks MCP1 and IL8 blocks plus an AC8 concentration-response section with no complement in it. Anyone recomputing a sheet-level count will get 380 and think the context is wrong. Also, and this is a real parsing trap: the C3a/C5a blocks use classical/alternative-pathway activator and inhibitor controls in columns B/C/D, whereas the MCP1/IL8 blocks use R848/CpG/poly-dC in those same columns. Column position does not identify the condition; the block header in column A must be read.

METHOD LESSONS FOR THE REMAINING RESOURCES:
- Field restriction is everything here. "complement activation" AND "antisense oligonucleotide" gave 663 hits of mostly 2026 reviews; TITLE:"complement" AND TITLE:"oligonucleotide" gave 14 hits of which 8 were on-target. Unrestricted boolean queries sort newest-first, so hit count is not a relevance signal.
- "Complement" as an ordinary VERB is the dominant false positive. PMID 36579950 matched on "small preliminary in vivo studies should also be considered to complement this early assessment" and PMID 35021888 on "complement UFH, rather than replace it"; both are not relevant. Any automated screen on the string "complement" needs this filter.
- Abstract-level screening MISSES real complement data. PMID 39252874's abstract names only aPTT and thrombocytopenia, yet its full text reports C3a ELISA in cynomolgus serum and human factor H binding. Full-text search is not optional for this endpoint.
- JOURNAL:"Nucleic Acid Therapeutics" as a sweep (65 hits) was efficient and surfaced the revusiran and GalNAc3 human-volunteer papers that analyte queries had missed.

- PATENTS FOUND BUT NOT COUNTED AS EVIDENCE, per the task rule that a patent describing an assay is not evidence the assay was run.
